purpose: Completed GC exclusion must end even while passive copies of its Unix flock descriptors remain open
baseline: a78cef1de80b16ed543536106f9c94d520340fcf, with an assertion added to the existing context/global lock test

before.result: FAILED: completed GC exclusion survived through duplicated descriptors
before.observation: Duplicate the local, legacy-global and legacy-context exclusive flock descriptors, drop the GC owner, then require a new GC guard while all passive copies remain open

fix: Owned exclusive Unix flock guards explicitly unlock on drop, including partial acquisition errors. GC record descriptors close before the flock guards; the same-process guard releases last. Cargo's inherited shared session descriptors retain their previous close-only lifetime.

after.requirements: Duplicated exclusion release, existing shared/global/legacy session protections and strict CAS-only pressure reclamation all pass

isolation: Each existing core case uses its own private temporary RGO_HOME; no developer activation changes. Descriptor duplication avoids forking a multithreaded test runner.
limits: This deterministic defect does not establish the cause of the earlier macOS beta CAS-reclamation failure. The corrected code passed all 19 individual platform jobs on the first attempt; that earlier failure remains unexplained. No Rust test case was added.

platform_lanes.macos_jobs: All four recorded jobs and all 19 individual matrix jobs completed successfully on attempt 1
